newsitem.title: UK: BAe expects talks with two US fighter bidders.
newsitem.headline: BAe expects talks with two US fighter bidders.

text.p: British Aerospace said on Monday it expected to have talks with both remaining bidders for the 100 billion pounds U.S. Joint Strike Fighter project, helping its shares on fresh hopes of BAe getting a slice of the deal.
BAe communications executive Mike Peter told Reuters "In relation to the Joint Strike Fighter (JSF), we expect to have talks with Lockheed Martin and Boeing."

Lockheed, one of the two final bidders to win the 3,000 aircraft contract, said it had already had discussions about a link-up with BAe. "Discussions have already been held and we expect more (to be held) in the future," said one spokesman.

Boeing was unavailable to comment on recent press speculation that it has spoken to the British group after weekend press reports that BAe was once again in the running for part of the JSF project after its last partner McDonnell Douglas was rejected.
The two remaining consortia, led by Lockheed Martin and Boeing, have been asked to build a prototype of the aircraft which will serve the U.S. Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps.
Both consortia will be tested out in a "fly-off" to be held by the U.S. government in roughly four years' time.
BAe can offer the two bidders its technical expertise in short take-off and vertical landing technology, as used in the Harrier jets.
The JSF factor was one reason behind a rise in BAe's share price on Monday after weakness last week related to the French government halting the sale of Thomson.

Another factor behind the strength was the hope that the sale of Thomson CSF, the defence arm, will eventually go ahead, allowing BAe to pursue the merger of its missile business with Thomson and Matra.
BAe was trading up 16 1/2 pence at 1119 pence by 1230 GMT.
